newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR says sugar workers agree jobs deal.
newsitem.headline: CSR says sugar workers agree jobs deal.

text.p: Diversified building products group CSR Ltd said on Monday that employees in its sugar division had voted to aprove an enterprise bargaining agreement.
"A vote has been taken and the majority of workers have approved (the agreement) but there is still a 14-day cooling off period," said Peter Frawley, CSR's executive general manager for sugar.
Frawley said under the agreement workers would receive an upfront two percent pay increase and further pay rises would be capped at 1.5 percent for the first year and two percent in subsequent years.
Speaking to reporters at a media briefing on the company's annual results, CSR's managing director Geoffrey Kells said CSR still considered its sugar operations a core investment.
"We are there for the long term in refined sugar and we believe that we have got ourselves to the lowest cost position in most of the markets that we are in," Kells said.
Kells said CSR was not threatened by the likely government scrapping of an import tariff on sugar expected to take effect from July 1 this year.
"It is up to market pressures whether it (the tariff cut) gets passed onto customers or not. On the question of imports, it is really up to us to hold a market position," he said.
"We think that we will be able to hold our position in the market against any import competition," he said.

CSR earlier said its earnings from sugar fell by 12 percent to A$74 million in the year to March 31, 1997. The company said its refined sugar business made a loss of A$7.2 million in 1996/97 compared to a loss of A$5.5 million the previous year.
